aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abel-maim.title: Abel-maim
abel-maim.note: Another name for Abel-beth-maachah, meaning Abel on the waters, and the form used when Asa hires Ben-hadad to attack Israel's northern towns. Assyria took the city about a century later, and Tiglath-pileser's own account of that campaign names it.

abiah.title: Abiah
abiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abiah.note: A name shared by kings, priests and Levites, which is why it covers so much ground. The one who gets the most space is Rehoboam's son, who ruled Judah for a short time and beat Jeroboam's army while badly outnumbered.

abihail-4.title: Abihail
abihail-4.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abihail-4.note: A wife of Rehoboam. She appears in a single verse.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

adnah.title: Adnah
adnah.note: Jehoshaphat's senior commander, at the head of 300,000 men, the largest single division named when the king reorganised his army.

adonijah-2.title: Adonijah
adonijah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adonijah-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

adoraim.title: Adoraim
adoraim.note: Rehoboam fortified it after the kingdom split, one link in Judah's southern line of defence. The name survives in Dura, a village southwest of Hebron.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

ahab.title: Ahab
ahab.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahab.note: King of northern Israel for about twenty-two years. He married Jezebel, a Phoenician princess. She brought Baal worship into a kingdom that was supposed to belong to Yahweh alone, and he let her.

ahaziah-2.title: Ahaziah
ahaziah-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaziah-2.note: He ruled northern Israel, fell through a palace lattice, and sent to a foreign god to ask about healing. Elijah rebuked him for not asking the Lord.

aijalon.title: Aijalon
aijalon.note: In the valley of Aijalon Joshua told the moon to stand still alongside the sun during the battle against the Amorite coalition. Later it marked the boundary of Danite and Benjamite territory.

amariah-5.title: Amariah
amariah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amariah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

amasiah.title: Amasiah
amasiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amasiah.note: In Jehoshaphat's army he commanded a thousand men, and he is remembered for volunteering himself for the LORD's service. Nothing further is recorded about him.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amon-2.title: Amon
amon-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon-2.note: 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

asa.title: Asa
asa.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asa.note: King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.

asahel-2.title: Asahel
asahel-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asahel-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

asaph.title: Asaph
asaph.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph.note: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.

attai-3.title: Attai
attai-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
attai-3.note: One of 3 men called Attai. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

azariah-12.title: Azariah
azariah-12.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-12.note: A prophet from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azubah-2.title: Azubah
azubah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azubah-2.note: Jehoshaphat's mother. Kings and Chronicles both name her in the notice of his reign and give her nothing more.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

baasha.title: Baasha
baasha.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baasha.note: He killed Nadab, Israel's second king, and wiped out the rest of Jeroboam's family to take the northern throne. That fulfilled a prophecy against Jeroboam's line. Baasha's own violence brought the same kind of end on his house.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

ben-hail.title: Ben-hail
ben-hail.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ben-hail.note: King Jehoshaphat sent him out, with priests and Levites, to teach the Book of the Law in the towns of Judah.

benaiah-7.title: Benaiah
benaiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benaiah-7.note: One of 12 men called Benaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

benhadad.title: Benhadad
benhadad.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benhadad.note: The name was a royal title in Aram-Damascus, carried by at least two kings and possibly three, all of them at war with Israel. This one is the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 15 and 20.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berachah-2.title: Berachah
berachah-2.note: The valley where Jehoshaphat's army blessed God after the battle, which is how it got the name.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-zur.title: Beth-zur
beth-zur.note: A fortified town in the hill country of Judah, a few miles north of Hebron. Rehoboam strengthened it as part of the defences of his kingdom once the ten northern tribes had broken away.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

chenaanah.title: Chenaanah
chenaanah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
chenaanah.note: His son Zedekiah was a false prophet who promised King Ahab victory and struck the true prophet Micaiah in the face for saying otherwise.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dodavah.title: Dodavah
dodavah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
dodavah.note: A man of Mareshah. His son Eliezer rebuked Jehoshaphat for joining Ahaziah of Israel in a shipbuilding venture, and God destroyed the ships.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eliab-2.title: Eliab
eliab-2.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
eliab-2.note: David's eldest brother. He was tall and looked the part, and Samuel thought he was the one until God told him the Lord looks at the heart. Later he tore into David for turning up at the Goliath battle line.

eliada-3.title: Eliada
eliada-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliada-3.note: One of 3 men called Eliada. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

eliezer-5.title: Eliezer
eliezer-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliezer-5.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

elishama-6.title: Elishama
elishama-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishama-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

en-gedi.title: En-gedi
en-gedi.note: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

etam-3.title: Etam
etam-3.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gerar.title: Gerar
gerar.note: Abraham and Isaac both stayed in this Philistine town in the Negev under a king called Abimelech, and both passed their wives off as sisters out of fear. Isaac reaped a hundredfold there and dug out his father's wells again until quarrels over water moved him on toward Beersheba. Tel Haror is a leading candidate for the site.

hanani.title: Hanani
hanani.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hanani.note: The prophet who went to King Asa and told him he had leaned on a foreign alliance instead of on God.

hazezon-tamar.title: Hazezon-tamar
hazezon-tamar.note: An Amorite town by the Dead Sea that Chedorlaomer's kings attacked in Abraham's day, later called En-gedi. The old name comes back in Jehoshaphat's reign, when Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites come up against Judah from there.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

iddo-2.title: Iddo
iddo-2.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
iddo-2.note: A seer whose writings Chronicles cites for the reigns of Solomon, Rehoboam and Abijah. The writings themselves are lost.

ijon.title: Ijon
ijon.note: In Naphtali, in Israel's far north. Ben-hadad took it at Asa's request, and later Tiglath-pileser III took it in Pekah's reign, a conquest his own inscriptions also list. It is usually identified with Tell Dibbin.

imla.title: Imla
imla.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
imla.note: Micaiah's father. Micaiah was the one prophet at Ahab's court who would contradict the four hundred and say Ahab would die in battle.

ishmael-4.title: Ishmael
ishmael-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ishmael-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jahaziel-4.title: Jahaziel
jahaziel-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jahaziel-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jehohanan-2.title: Jehohanan
jehohanan-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehohanan-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehoram-2.title: Jehoram
jehoram-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoram-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehoshaphat.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshaphat.note: A king of Judah who sent officials and Levites through the land to teach the law. His alliance with Israel kept going wrong, and in one battle enemy soldiers took him for Ahab and nearly killed him. When Moab, Ammon and Edom invaded together, he sent singers ahead of the army, and the invaders destroyed each other.

jehozabad-3.title: Jehozabad
jehozabad-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehozabad-3.note: One of 3 men called Jehozabad. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

jehu-2.title: Jehu
jehu-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehu-2.note: A prophet, not the king of the same name. In Kings he speaks judgment against a king of Israel, and in Chronicles he rebukes a southern king and writes up that king's reign.

jehush-5.title: Jehush
jehush-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehush-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

jeiel-4.title: Jeiel
jeiel-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jermoth-6.title: Jermoth
jermoth-6.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
jermoth-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jeroboam.title: Jeroboam
jeroboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
jeroboam.note: Solomon's official who led the ten northern tribes out after Rehoboam refused to lighten the labour his father had laid on them. To stop his people going back to Jerusalem to worship, he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan with a priesthood of his own. Every northern king after him gets measured against that sin.

jeruel.title: Jeruel
jeruel.note: Wilderness on the climb from the Dead Sea up toward Jerusalem, near Tekoa. Jehoshaphat's army met a coalition of Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites there and never had to fight, because God turned the invaders on each other.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jeshanah.title: Jeshanah
jeshanah.note: Abijah of Judah captured this northern town from Jeroboam, with Bethel and Ephron, in a battle Judah won though badly outnumbered. It is generally identified with Burj el-Isaneh, north of Bethel. Nehemiah's Jeshanah gate in Jerusalem is a different thing.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

joash-4.title: Joash
joash-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

kohathites.title: Kohathites
kohathites.about: Levi's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kohathites.note: One of the three Levitical divisions, descended from Kohath. They carried the holiest furnishings, the ark among them, on poles and not in a cart, and 2 Samuel 6 shows what happened when that rule was broken. They camped south of the tabernacle. Moses, Aaron and Samuel were all Kohathites.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

maachah.title: Maachah
maachah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
maachah.note: Absalom's granddaughter, married to Rehoboam, and queen mother after him. Her grandson Asa took the title away because she promoted idol worship.

mahalath-2.title: Mahalath
mahalath-2.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mahalath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a woman from the divided-kingdom years.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

mareshah.title: Mareshah
mareshah.note: Rehoboam fortified this Shephelah city, and Asa beat Zerah the Cushite's far larger army there. Micah mourns it among Judah's towns. Its ruins at Tell Sandahanna hold a Hellenistic underground city and painted Sidonian tombs full of exotic animals.

mattaniah-4.title: Mattaniah
mattaniah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattaniah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

micah.title: Micah
micah.note: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.

michaiah-2.title: Michaiah
michaiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
michaiah-2.note: One of the officials Jehoshaphat sent round Judah to teach the law.

michaiah.title: Michaiah
michaiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michaiah.note: Mother of King Abijah of Judah, probably the woman called Maacah elsewhere.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

naamah.title: Naamah
naamah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
naamah.note: An Ammonite, one of Solomon's foreign wives, and the mother of Rehoboam, the only one of Solomon's wives named as a king's mother.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebat.title: Nebat
nebat.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nebat.note: Jeroboam's father, and he is only ever named in "Jeroboam son of Nebat," the phrase the books of Kings use again and again for the king blamed for making idol worship the habit of the north.

nethaneel-6.title: Nethaneel
nethaneel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaneel-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

nethaniah-3.title: Nethaniah
nethaniah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaniah-3.note: One of 4 men called Nethaniah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

obadiah-9.title: Obadiah
obadiah-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
obadiah-9.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

oded.title: Oded
oded.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
oded.note: His son Azariah was the prophet who encouraged King Asa's reforms. Oded himself is only ever a father's name in 2 Chronicles 15.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramoth-gilead.title: Ramoth-gilead
ramoth-gilead.note: A city of refuge in Gad's land east of the Jordan, and too useful for Israel and Aram to leave alone. Ahab died after being wounded there trying to take it back with Jehoshaphat.

rehoboam.title: Rehoboam
rehoboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
rehoboam.note: Solomon's son, and he lost most of the kingdom in his first days on the throne. The northern tribes asked him to lighten the heavy labour his father had laid on them. He turned down the older advisers and threatened them with worse.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

shamariah-2.title: Shamariah
shamariah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shamariah-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shelomith-5.title: Shelomith
shelomith-5.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelomith-5.note: A woman from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shemaiah-12.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-12.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-12.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shemaiah.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
shemaiah.note: The prophet who stopped Rehoboam from going to war with the northern tribes after the split. He said the division was God's own doing.

shemiramoth-2.title: Shemiramoth
shemiramoth-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemiramoth-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shilhi.title: Shilhi
shilhi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shilhi.note: His daughter Azubah married King Asa and was the mother of King Jehoshaphat, and that is why he is named.

shishak.title: Shishak
shishak.about: Pharaoh living at the time of United Monarchy
shishak.note: The pharaoh who invaded Judah in Rehoboam's reign and stripped Solomon's temple of its treasures. He put the campaign on a relief at Karnak, listing the towns.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

sukkiims.title: Sukkiims
sukkiims.note: They marched with Shishak's Egyptian army when it invaded Judah in Rehoboam's fifth year, alongside Libyans and Cushites. The name likely means tent-dwellers.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tekoa.title: Tekoa
tekoa.note: It sat about six miles south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness that carries its name. Rehoboam fortified it, and Amos was a herdsman there when he was called to prophesy against Israel.

tob-adonijah.title: Tob-adonijah
tob-adonijah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tob-adonijah.note: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent around the cities of Judah with priests and other Levites, teaching from the Book of the Law.

tobiah.title: Tobiah
tobiah.about: Nehemiah's adversary living at the time of Exile and Return
tobiah.note: They called him the Ammonite. With Sanballat he mocked Nehemiah's wall and worked against it, and later a priest gave him a room inside the temple courts, so Nehemiah threw him and his things out.

uriel-3.title: Uriel
uriel-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
uriel-3.note: One of 3 men called Uriel. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Chronicles.

zachariah-10.title: Zachariah
zachariah-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-10.note: One of 29 men called Zachariah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles. The verse is 2 Chronicles 20:14.

zachariah-9.title: Zachariah
zachariah-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-9.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years. The verse is 2 Chronicles 17:7.

zaham.title: Zaham
zaham.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zaham.note: Rehoboam's son by Abihail, and that is all of him.

zarah-6.title: Zarah
zarah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zarah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

zareah.title: Zareah
zareah.note: Samson's hometown, better known as Zorah, on the border of Judah and Dan. The angel of the Lord told Manoah's wife there that she would have a son, and Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.

zebadiah-6.title: Zebadiah
zebadiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zebadiah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

zebadiah-7.title: Zebadiah
zebadiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zebadiah-7.note: One of 9 men called Zebadiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

zedekiah-2.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah-2.note: A different Zedekiah from the king. He is the man in 1 Kings 22 and 2 Chronicles 18 who stood with the court prophets, and struck the one prophet who disagreed.

zemaraim.title: Zemaraim
zemaraim.note: Two places. One is a town of Benjamin, generally put at a ruin north of Jericho. The other is a hill in Ephraim where Abijah of Judah beat Jeroboam's much bigger army.

zichri-7.title: Zichri
zichri-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zichri-7.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

ziph.title: Ziph
ziph.note: David hid in the wilderness around Ziph, southeast of Hebron, while Saul was hunting him. The people of Ziph told Saul where he was, twice.

ziz.title: Ziz
ziz.note: The Moabites and Ammonites came up against Jehoshaphat by the ascent of Ziz, a pass near En-gedi on the Dead Sea. It is generally identified with a steep track climbing toward Tekoa.

ziza-2.title: Ziza
ziza-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ziza-2.note: A son of Rehoboam. The other Ziza is a Simeonite prince who took land at Gedor.
